root-causes:
- (a) `plugin.test.ts` compared `AGENTS = join(...)` with a `/` string. On Windows `join` gives backslashes (the log shows `packages\integrations\...`). The test now compares `toPosix(AGENTS)`. A second assertion builds the path with `win32.join` and `toPosix(..., "\\")`, so the Windows form is checked on Linux too.
- (b) The log shows only a plain 5000ms timeout, with nothing else wrong. The test runs about 30 CLI starts in a row (14 dispatches, 14 records, 2 hooks). Each start costs more on Windows, so the run passes the default. It takes 3.6s on Linux. I gave it a 40_000ms timeout, the same as the other long hook test, and added a comment. I found no cause in the code to fix instead.
- (c) `host.test.ts` called `isExecutable(wrapper, "linux")`. That makes `stat` read the real file, and NTFS has no execute bit, so it returned false. I split the test in two:
  - A new test calls `isExecutable` with the real platform and runs everywhere. It is the committed mode on Windows and the execute bit on POSIX.
  - The original `"linux"` test is kept and skipped on win32 only.

The win32 skip is for behavior that does not exist on Windows (POSIX execute bits). A comment says so. The production branch exists as the `platform === "win32"` branch of `isExecutable` in `tests/host.ts`, and the existing test "is the mode the repository commits for it on Windows" already checks it on Linux.
